units.title: Business 1: business activity, marketing and people

outcomes.text: Explain the purpose of business activity: spotting an opportunity, developing an idea and meeting customer needs.
Describe the characteristics of an entrepreneur: creativity, risk taking, determination and confidence.
Explain the concept of risk and reward.
Explain why businesses plan: to reduce risk and help the business succeed.
Explain the role and usefulness of a business plan in identifying markets, getting finance, finding resources and meeting aims.
Describe sole traders, partnerships, and private and public limited companies.
Explain limited liability.
Judge which type of ownership suits start-ups and established businesses.
Describe business aims and objectives: profit, survival, growth, providing a service and market share.
Explain how and why objectives change as businesses evolve.
Explain why different businesses have different objectives.
Describe the roles and objectives of internal and external stakeholders: owners, employees, customers, suppliers, government and the local community.
Explain the effect of business activity on stakeholders.
Explain the effect stakeholders have on a business.
Explain organic growth through more output, new customers, new products and more market share.
Explain external growth through mergers and takeovers, including horizontal, vertical and diversification.
Explain why marketing matters: knowing customers, informing them and raising sales.
Explain the purpose of market research in understanding customer needs.
Describe primary research: questionnaires, interviews, trialling and focus groups.
Describe secondary research sources: newspapers, magazines, census, websites and internal data.
Judge how suitable different methods and sources are for different purposes.
Use and interpret qualitative and quantitative market research data.
Explain how segmenting by age, gender, income, location and lifestyle helps target customers.
Name the four Ps of the marketing mix (price, product, place, promotion) and why they matter.
Describe product design, invention and innovation.
Describe the stages of the product life cycle: introduction, growth, maturity and decline.
Explain pricing methods: skimming, cost-plus, penetration, competitor and promotional.
Describe point-of-sale promotion: price reductions, loss leaders, competitions and free samples.
Describe advertising through social media, websites, print, television and radio.
Describe place: digital and physical distribution channels.
Explain how the four Ps work together and inform business decisions.
Interpret market data on demand, target market, market share, product changes and the effects of promotion.
Explain how human resources identifies and meets a business's staffing needs.

subtopics.title: 3.2 Organisational structures and ways of working

outcomes.text: Compare tall and flat organisational structures.
Use organisation chart terms: span of control, chain of command, delegation, subordinates and authority.
Explain why businesses use different structures, linked to communication, job roles and ways of working.
Describe full-time, part-time, flexible, temporary, home, mobile and self-employed working.
Describe ways to communicate: letter, email, text, phone, meeting, presentation, social media and website.
Explain why business communication matters.
Explain how digital communication influences business activity.
Explain why businesses recruit: replacing leavers, growth and skill gaps.
Compare internal and external recruitment, job descriptions and person specifications.
Describe selection methods: CV, application form, letter, interview, tests, group activities and references.
Describe financial motivation: pay, bonuses, profit sharing and fringe benefits.
Describe non-financial motivation: praise, award schemes and working environment.
Explain why motivation improves performance and helps retention.
Explain why retaining staff saves recruitment time and expense.
Compare induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training.
Explain why businesses train: development, productivity, skill shortages, service, motivation and retention.
Describe staff development through vocational and academic qualifications and apprenticeships.
Explain the benefits of staff development to employees and businesses.
Explain how law on discrimination, contracts, holidays and hours of work affects recruitment and employment.

units.title: Business 2: operations, finance and influences on business

outcomes.text: Compare job, batch and flow production and their impact on businesses.
Explain how automation, computers and robotics change production.
Explain the concept of quality.
Compare quality control and quality assurance.
Explain why quality protects reputation, wins and keeps customers, and cuts returns and recalls.
Describe selling by e-commerce, face to face and telesales.
Explain how e-commerce influences business activity.
Explain why good customer service, including after-sales, wins and keeps customers.
Explain how product knowledge and customer engagement support good service.
Explain how consumer law, on safety and satisfactory quality, affects business reputation.
Explain how costs, nearness to market, labour and materials influence location.
Describe procurement: identifying needs, choosing suppliers, ordering and receiving deliveries.
Explain how logistics and supply choices affect time, supply chain length, reliability, costs and service.

subtopics.title: 5.1 The role of the finance function

outcomes.text: Explain how finance provides information and supports planning and decisions.
Explain how the finance function influences business activity.
Explain why businesses need finance: start-up, expansion, running costs, recruitment and marketing.
Describe loans, overdrafts, trade credit, retained profit, sale of assets, owners' capital, new partners, share issues and crowdfunding.
Judge which sources suit new and established businesses.
Explain revenue, costs and profit or loss and why they matter in decisions.
Tell fixed, variable and total costs apart.
Calculate costs, revenue and profit or loss, including gross and net profit.
Calculate and interpret gross and net profit margins.
Calculate and interpret average rate of return.
Explain break-even as the point where total costs equal total revenue.
Calculate break-even quantity.
Explain how break-even informs marketing and planning decisions.
Explain why cash gives liquidity to meet short-term debts.
Tell cash from profit.
Explain how cash flow forecasts help planning, warn of shortages, allow remedies and provide targets.
Complete a cash flow forecast.
Explain how ethical issues, such as treatment of workers, sourcing and marketing, affect businesses.
Explain how sustainability, waste, pollution and climate change affect businesses.
Explain how changing consumer income and unemployment affect businesses.
Explain globalisation.
Explain its impact on multinationals, location, international branding and international competition.
Explain how operations, finance, marketing and human resources depend on each other.
Explain how these interdependencies shape business decisions.
Explain the impact of risk and reward on business activity.
Use financial information to measure performance and support decisions.
